newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria edges up as Brady market awaits U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria edges up as Brady market awaits U.S. data.

text.p: Bulgaria managed to continue its modest recovery on Friday in a very subdued emerging debt market which is waiting to see the impact of U.S. data later in the day.
"Bulgaria is a bit firmer, but volume is very thin," a U.S. bank trader said.
Bulgarian IABs were bid at 48-1/8 cents in the dollar, about two points above the low they plunged to on Wednesday after President Petar Stoyanov warned of a possible default on debt servicing.
A number of analysts have long told their investors to stick to options if they want Bulgarian debt.
Most expect continued sharp volatility in the debt's price, which has tumbled more than 10 percent in just over a week, until there are some signs of political and economic stability.
But ANZ analyst Jerome Booth said Bulgaria was a clear buy at the latest low levels.
He noted that Bulgaria had paid its January Brady coupon and that the next payment was not due until July 28.
"Whilst political uncertainty is set to persist for the next few weeks, and may induce some further temporary weakness, the political crisis may be nearing an end," Booth said.
There are signs that the ruling Socialists would concede to demands for early elections in the face of major public unrest.

Early elections would see the reformist Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) gain a sweeping mandate to implement reform, with the International Monetary Fund coming up with the funds to put a currency board in place, he added.
The rest of the market barely traded waiting for this afternoon's U.S. fourth quarter gdp figures.
